story_scenes.1: It is Mona's first Monday at RetailCo India. CEO Chinnu walks her to a whiteboard covered in sticky notes — North, South, East, West, Central — and says: "We sell snacks and drinks across India, but I still get five different Excel files every week. I need one place to see the truth. That's why you're here — and that's what SAP Analytics Cloud will become for us." Before Mona touches any software today, she needs to understand the world Chinnu lives in.
story_scenes.2: Chinnu forwards Mona an email with a link: "Your SAC trial is ready — tenant URL inside. Log in and explore; break things if you need to." Mona opens https://[tenant].us10.hcs.cloud.sap, heart beating a little fast. The home screen lists Stories, Models, Connections — menus she's never seen. Chinnu calls: "Don't worry — everyone feels lost on Day 1. Find Stories and Models first. Today is about object types and connection mechanics, not perfection."
story_scenes.3: Menon sends Mona a WhatsApp: "Can you tell me our beverage numbers for March? I have them in a CSV somewhere…" Minutes later, Nandan from Finance forwards the same figures as an Excel attachment: "Please stop us emailing this every month." Mona sees the pattern — Date, Region, Product, Revenue, Units, Target — scattered across files. Today she imports RetailCo's sales CSV into SAC, maps columns to dimensions and measures, and builds her first Analytic Model. Get the totals wrong by ₹1 and every dashboard for two weeks lies.
story_scenes.4: Chinnu opens a draft dashboard Mona built from yesterday's model and frowns: "I see total revenue, but are we hitting target? Which region is behind? Put India on a map — and Menon keeps asking why he can see North's numbers. Fix all of that today." Raw imports aren't enough. Mona adds calculated measures (% vs Target, YTD), geo enrichment for a regional map, and Data Access Control so Menon sees South only.
story_scenes.5: It is Monday morning. Chinnu's ritual: coffee, laptop, dashboard. He wants three answers in ten seconds — "How much did we sell? Who is winning? Are we growing?" Today Mona builds Page 1 of his executive story: three big KPI tiles, a region bar chart, a monthly trend line, and dropdown filters. This is the page that earns her trust.
story_scenes.6: Menon calls Mona: "South looks good on Page 1, but which snack SKUs are actually driving it? I don't want another report request — I want to click and see." Static dashboards won't cut it. Today Mona adds Page 2, configures linked analysis from the region bar chart, enables drilldown, turns on Smart Insights, and exports PDF for Chinnu's board pack.
story_scenes.7: Nandan from Finance emails Mona a thick Excel file, CC'ing Chinnu: "This is our FY2026 budget — five regions, three categories, twelve months. We email versions back and forth until someone overwrites the wrong tab. Can SAC be our one budget workbook that never breaks?" Welcome to Planning — where numbers get typed in and saved, not just viewed.
story_scenes.8: Nandan sighs on a Friday call: "Every month I copy last month's actuals, add 10% growth for South, and spread COGS across products by hand. It takes Finance all afternoon." Mona builds him a Data Action button: one click, done. Nandan thinks she's magic — she's just automating what Finance used to do by hand.
story_scenes.9: Month-end at RetailCo is controlled chaos — load actuals, refresh forecast, let planners adjust, lock approved numbers, email Chinnu. Mona asks him: "Can this run itself on the first of every month?" Today she chains steps into a Multi Action and puts it on the Planning Calendar. She is no longer building reports — she is designing how the company thinks.
story_scenes.10: The warehouse manager in Hyderabad calls: "We're overstocked on cola in South but understocked on chips in East. Can you tell us what the next three months look like?" Chinnu tells Mona: "Use Smart Predict — show me a forecast with a range, not a guess." Today SAC becomes a crystal ball backed by maths.
story_scenes.11: Chinnu schedules a 10 AM review: "Show me everything we've built for RetailCo. Pretend I'm the board." Mona's stomach flutters — good flutters. Today she polishes three story pages, exports a PDF, practices her narrative out loud, and sketches a path toward SAP certification. This is her graduation day for Phase 1–4.
story_scenes.12: IT sends Mona a diagram: "In production we don't use CSV uploads — sales flows S/4HANA → Datasphere → SAC live. Your training import was practice wheels. Time for the real bicycle." Today she learns how RetailCo's live architecture keeps Chinnu's Monday dashboard always fresh without copying millions of rows.
story_scenes.13: Mona maps the integration puzzle for Chinnu: "Finance actuals come from S/4HANA, travel expenses from Concur, old history still lives in BW, and daily sales in Datasphere. Can one SAC tenant talk to all of them?" Yes — but each source speaks a different connection language. Today she draws the full family tree.
story_scenes.14: Go-live week. Two hundred users will open Mona's dashboard on Monday. Chinnu's last question: "Will it load fast? Will South managers see only South? Can we move this from test to production safely?" Today Mona answers with weightage analysis, security roles, and a go-live checklist. She is ready.
